html:
The Balkan Wars were two wars in 1912 and 1913 that ended almost five centuries of Ottoman rule in the Balkans and divided the region of Macedonia among Serbia, Greece and Bulgaria.

In the First Balkan War, from October 1912, Serbia, Greece, Bulgaria and Montenegro attacked the Ottomans. The Serbs won at Kumanovo and took Skopje. In the Second, in summer 1913, Bulgaria turned on its allies over the spoils and lost. The Treaty of Bucharest gave Serbia most of today's North Macedonia, Greece the south and Bulgaria a smaller part. Albania was created. The wars brought massacres and mass flight of Muslims and Christians, and left Serbia stronger and Austria alarmed, a step toward World War I.
sum: The Balkan Wars were two wars in 1912 and 1913 that ended almost five centuries of Ottoman rule in the Balkans and divided the region of Macedonia among Serbia, Greece and Bulgaria.
